messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D Ludo game for phones and tablets.

## Requirements
- Deliver a playable game now; do not ask clarifying questions.
- Support responsive phone/tablet layouts and usable touch controls.
- Briefly note assumptions when finishing.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide) and inspect only the latest.

## Decisions
- Implemented a single-player game against three computer opponents.
- Used Three.js via CDN for the 3D board and tokens.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game UI, responsive styling, 3D board, tokens, dice flow, turn handling, CPU turns, captures, finishing, and help/new-game controls.
- Repaired a JavaScript module-scope error by consolidating code into `game.js`.
- `node --check game.js` passes.

### Active
- Validate the browser rendering and gameplay; fix any issues discovered.
- Take and inspect a current small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- Browser initially reported `ReferenceError: COLORS is not defined` after the module was split; this was fixed, but browser validation has not yet been rerun.

## Next Move
1. Reload `http://localhost:3002` in the open Playwright session and check console errors.
2. Save and inspect a JPEG screenshot; test dice/token interactions, mobile layout, and new game.
3. Fix issues found and report the single-player-versus-CPU assumption.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game page, controls, status panel, and help dialog.
- `styles.css`: Desktop and mobile/tablet layouts and visual styling.
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, board construction, game rules, CPU behavior, and interactions.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- A local server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- Playwright initially opened successfully but recorded the `COLORS is not defined` error before the correction.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D Ludo game for phones and tablets.

## Requirements
- Deliver a playable game without clarifying questions; briefly note assumptions when finishing.
- Support responsive phone/tablet layouts and usable touch controls.

- Implemented single-player Ludo against three computer opponents.
